title: Felix and the Debt
premise: Noor Okonkwo, a private security contractor who has spent seven years erasing himself from every database, receives a meeting invitation from his handler, Marcus Vey — dead for three weeks. The invitation leads him to a dead-drop containing proof that the private intelligence firm they both served, Halcyon Verity, has been laundering assassinations through three governments' counterterrorism budgets. Pursued by Halcyon's cleaner, an assassin called the Cartographer who maps victims before killing them, Noor must assemble a network of the discarded — a disgraced auditor, a whistleblower widow, and his estranged sister in Lagos — to move the truth past three governments that all want it buried. The climax comes when Noor trades himself to the Cartographer to buy time for the leak, discovering the assassin is another erased contractor following the same rewritten rules. In the end, the files detonate across three capitals, Halcyon burns, and Noor — finally visible, finally accountable — surrenders to a court that may or may not be just, choosing inheritance of consequence over the comfort of invisibility.
about_author: Lior Vane is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients he was never allowed to name. He writes thrillers about people whose jobs require them to not exist.

chapters.title: The Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Working a routine protection detail in Rotterdam, Noor receives a calendar invite from Marcus Vey, his handler, confirmed dead three weeks ago. The invite is timestamped tomorrow, 6 a.m., with coordinates. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in grief — the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Rewriting
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Flashback woven into present: seven years of protocol, burn bags, and names he never learned. He checks the coordinates against old tradecraft and realizes the drop pattern is one only Vey taught him. Beat: reluctant loyalty — he decides to go, telling himself it's due diligence.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at Dawn
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At an abandoned tram depot, Noor finds a burner phone, a keycard, and a photograph of himself he never posed for. The phone holds one encrypted file labeled DEBT. Beat: cold fear — someone has been watching the man whose job was to be unwatchable.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Draws First
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV. Introduced without name: a meticulous killer who sketches maps of his targets' lives before ending them. He notes that Noor took the bait faster than projected. Beat: clinical menace — the hunt begins as paperwork.

chapters.title: Halcyon Verity
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Using Vey's keycard, Noor enters a Halcyon archive annex in Antwerp and finds ledgers linking contract killings to counterterrorism line items in three national budgets. Beat: vertigo — the rules he obeyed were the crime.

chapters.title: What Vey Owed
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A hidden memo reveals Vey discovered the laundering months ago and started copying files; his 'accidental' death now reads as execution. The word DEBT recurs — Vey's code for what Halcyon owes its victims. Beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Reverse
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Halcyon flags Noor's access; his accounts freeze, his safehouses burn remotely. Seven years of invisibility evaporates in an hour. Beat: exposure panic — the invisible man suddenly lit up on every screen.

chapters.title: The Auditor Who Wouldn't Sign
chapters.summary: Ilse Brandt's POV. A disgraced EU forensic auditor, fired for asking about the same budget lines, recognizes patterns in leaked fragments reaching her inbox. She doesn't know who's sending them. Beat: cautious hope — two erased people circling each other.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor decodes enough of DEBT to see all three governments were both client and cover — each believed it was buying deniability, none knew it was funding murder. Beat: disillusionment; there is no clean side to run to.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Noor contacts Ilse through a cutout; she tests him with a false detail he corrects, proving he's read the real ledgers. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: trust as calculated risk.

chapters.title: The Widow's Testimony
chapters.summary: Amara Diallo's POV. In Brussels, the widow of a journalist killed by a 'terrorist cell' that never existed gives Ilse a recorded confession trail. Her grief becomes evidence. Beat: sorrow transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Map of a Man
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV. The Cartographer completes his sketch of Noor: habits, debts, the sister in Lagos he hasn't called in four years. He books a flight. Beat: intimate violation — the hunter knows Noor better than anyone alive.

chapters.title: Sister in Surulere
chapters.summary: Adaeze Okonkwo's POV. In Lagos, Adaeze — a human rights lawyer — gets a call from a brother she'd written off, asking for help she can't legally give. Beat: fractured belonging; family as unfinished business.

chapters.title: The Lagos Option
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor flies to Lagos, believing the safest vault for DEBT is a courtroom, not a server. En route he spots surveillance too good to be coincidence. Beat: paranoia sharpening into clarity — the Cartographer isn't following, he's herding.

chapters.title: Ambush at Murtala Muhammed
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Airport ambush; Noor escapes by triggering a crowd panic he hates himself for causing. He loses the physical copy of half the ledger. Beat: guilt and survival entangled — every escape costs innocents something.

chapters.title: Adaeze's Terms
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Adaeze agrees to help only if everything goes through lawful channels eventually — no leaks without witnesses, no justice outside accountability. Noor resists; he trusts neither courts nor governments. Beat: thematic collision — inheritance versus invention of justice.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse finds Vey's backup ledger hidden in a Rotterdam storage unit under Noor's own alias — Vey trusted no one but the man he never warned. Beat: posthumous betrayal and tenderness at once; Vey used him and saved him.

chapters.title: Cleaners in the Canal District
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Halcyon cleaners hit the storage unit minutes after Noor leaves with the ledger. A neighbor dies. Beat: the body count makes the abstract concrete — this debt is paid in blood.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Offer
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV. The Cartographer contacts Noor directly: surrender the ledger, and Adaeze and Ilse go unmapped. He sends a sketch of Adaeze's office as proof of reach. Beat: terror weaponized through intimacy.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor refuses, moving Adaeze to a safehouse and lying to her about why. She sees through it instantly. Beat: love expressed as deception, and its cost.

chapters.title: Government One: The Denial
chapters.summary: Minister's aide POV (unnamed). Inside a European interior ministry, officials confirm the ledger is authentic and begin quietly destroying documents rather than addressing them. Beat: institutional cowardice — the state protecting itself from its own signature.

chapters.title: Government Two: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. A second government offers Ilse immunity and a professorship for the ledger originals. She records the offer. Beat: temptation made bureaucratic; corruption wearing a lanyard.

chapters.title: Government Three: The Old Debt
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor traces the oldest entry in the ledger to a massacre fifteen years ago — one Vey helped cover, one Noor unknowingly guarded the witnesses against. His inheritance of complicity lands. Beat: devastating recognition — he was part of it.

chapters.title: Confession to Adaeze
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Noor tells his sister everything, including his own small role. She doesn't forgive him; she tells him forgiveness isn't hers to give — the victims hold that debt. Beat: grace without absolution.

chapters.title: The Network of the Discarded
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs briefly. Whistleblowers, ex-contractors, and journalists form a relay to authenticate and distribute DEBT across jurisdictions so no single government can bury it. Beat: solidarity rising — belonging built from the erased.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Relay
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. One relay member is turned; a safehouse falls, Ilse barely escapes, and the distribution schedule leaks. Beat: paranoia returns, but the network holds anyway — trust wounded, not broken.

chapters.title: Vey's Last Message
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The burner phone unlocks a final video: Vey, knowing he'd die, explains the DEBT metaphor — 'they wrote us off as expenses; make them audit their souls.' Beat: grief resolved into inheritance; Noor accepts the mission as legacy.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Set Both Ways
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV. The Cartographer realizes Halcyon plans to erase him too once Noor is dead — his own map shows his name on the next page. Beat: the instrument seeing itself as target; first crack in his certainty.

chapters.title: Negotiation on Neutral Ground
chapters.summary: Alternating Noor/Cartographer POV. In a Trieste warehouse, hunter and hunted meet. Noor offers the Cartographer a place in the testimony — a way out of being an expense. Beat: dangerous empathy between two men built by the same machine.

chapters.title: Halcyon Closes the Account
chapters.summary: Halcyon director POV. The board orders total asset liquidation: kill everyone exposed, including the Cartographer, and torch the archives. Beat: banality of evil at boardroom scale.

chapters.title: The Archive Fire
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse races to preserve physical records ahead of the burn, salvaging the massacre file — the one that implicates all three governments equally. Beat: rescue as resistance; paper outlasting power.

chapters.title: Sacrifice Play
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. To draw Halcyon's teams away from the distribution, Noor lets himself be captured, trading his body for the network's hour of head start. Beat: deliberate self-erasure inverted — becoming visible as a weapon.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In a black site, Noor endures interrogation, giving nothing while stalling for the release window. He recites victim names aloud until his interrogators flinch. Beat: endurance as moral act; the debt spoken into the room.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Changes Sides
chapters.summary: Cartographer's POV. Sent to kill Noor, the Cartographer instead kills his own handlers and frees him, handing over his complete map of Halcyon's operations. Beat: redemption without softness — he does it as payment, not virtue.

chapters.title: Detonation
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. DEBT goes live simultaneously in three countries: parliaments convene, ministers resign, warrants issue. Broadcasts carry Amara's widow testimony and the massacre file. Beat: catharsis — truth breaking through like floodwater.

chapters.title: The Fall of Halcyon Verity
chapters.summary: Director POV. The board scatters; the director is arrested at a private airfield holding a passport that no longer works anywhere. Beat: cold justice — the machinery devouring its makers.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Adaeze secures a plea framework: full disclosure in exchange for trial, not amnesty. Noor must stand in open court and be seen. Beat: the theme crystallized — justice requires visibility, and visibility requires courage.

chapters.title: The Trial of Noor Okonkwo
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor testifies for nine days, naming every operation, including his own complicity. The Cartographer testifies masked beside him. Beat: reckoning — inheritance accepted, debt publicly accounted.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Convicted on lesser counts, sentenced to six years; the governments fall into scandal; victims' families receive restitution funds carved from frozen Halcyon assets. Beat: imperfect justice honored as still worth having.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Noor and Adaeze POV, closing scene. Visiting hours at a low-security prison: Adaeze brings case files of families still fighting; Noor, finally a man with a record instead of a ghost, begins helping. Beat: quiet resolution — belonging found not in invisibility, but in accountability shared.
